topic: Research: Multi-Agent Framework Comparison 2026: LangGraph vs CrewAI vs ADK vs Strands vs Agno

key_points: Compares a broad set of open-source agent frameworks, including LangGraph, CrewAI, Google ADK, Strands Agents, and Agno.
Frames the core tradeoff as autonomy versus structure for production reliability.

Positions LangGraph for explicit graph control, CrewAI for role-based collaboration, ADK for Google/Gemini ecosystems, Strands for model-agnostic production agents with OpenTelemetry, and Agno for SDK plus managed platform convenience.
Recent 2026 comparison focused on production readiness, observability, debugging, ecosystem fit, and pricing transparency.
Recommends LangGraph for stateful multi-agent orchestration and complex agents requiring precision.
Positions CrewAI as the fast path for role-based prototypes and Google ADK as a GCP-native, batteries-included agent runtime.
Compares leading multi-agent frameworks through coordination primitives, state persistence, model dependency, and use cases.
Emphasizes that framework choice determines how agents share state, handle failures, and recover from orchestration mistakes.
Highlights CrewAI as beginner-friendly and LangGraph as stronger for production control; includes ADK but not Agno or Strands as primary entries.
Developer-oriented comparison updated June 10, 2026 with practical guidance for CrewAI, LangGraph, Mastra, CopilotKit, AutoGen, and Claude Code.
Offers a clear LangGraph-versus-CrewAI rule: LangGraph for explicit state, branches, retries, checkpoints, and resumability; CrewAI for role-based pipelines and fastest prototypes.
Useful competitive gap: does not deeply cover Google ADK, Strands, or Agno, leaving room for this article to own the cloud/runtime comparison.
Enterprise-oriented overview of AI agent frameworks, especially LangGraph, CrewAI, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, AutoGen, and OpenAI Swarm.
Explains selection around workflow complexity, data management, integration needs, and organizational fit.
Competitive gap: older framework lineup omits newer production/runtime players such as Strands Agents, Google ADK 2.x, and Agno 2.x.

PwC's May 2025 survey of 300 senior executives found 79% said AI agents were already being adopted, 88% planned AI budget increases due to agentic AI, and 66% of adopters reported measurable productivity value.
GitHub's Octoverse 2025 reported more than 1.1 million public repositories using an LLM SDK and 693,867 of those projects created in the prior 12 months, up 178% year over year.
Official ADK positioning in 2026 includes multi-agent orchestration, graph-based workflows, performance evaluation, and enterprise deployment for scalability and reliability.
Official Strands documentation describes three primary multi-agent patterns: Graph, Swarm, and Workflow, each chosen by control needs, determinism, cycles, parallel execution, and error handling.
Official Agno docs describe support for agents, multi-agent teams, step-based workflows, AgentOS APIs, isolated sessions, tracing, scheduling, RBAC, and audit logs.

angles: Do not crown a universal winner; frame the article as a production decision matrix based on state, orchestration style, cloud lock-in, observability, language/runtime, and team maturity.
The 2026 shift is from agent demos to governed, resumable systems. Evaluation, traceability, RBAC, audit logs, and failure recovery matter more than prompt ergonomics.
LangGraph is the control-plane choice for explicit state machines, branches, loops, retries, human checkpoints, and resumable workflows.
CrewAI is the fastest way to express role-based work, especially research, writing, analyst, sales, and ops pipelines where the team metaphor is natural.
Google ADK is best framed as the GCP/Gemini-native option: strong if the buyer already wants Google deployment, debugging UIs, graph workflows, and enterprise services.
Strands Agents deserves a production/AWS angle: model-driven agents, model-provider flexibility, OpenTelemetry, and patterns for graph, swarm, and workflow orchestration.
Agno is no longer just a lightweight Python agent library; position it as an agent platform/runtime layer with AgentOS, APIs, tracing, scheduling, RBAC, and audit logs.
Use popularity carefully: CrewAI leads this set by GitHub stars, but newer cloud-native runtimes like ADK and Strands can matter more in enterprise architecture decisions.
A strong unique insight: many real production teams will combine frameworks, for example LangGraph or ADK for orchestration, Strands for AWS-native tools, and Agno for runtime/control-plane concerns.
Include an honest 'avoid this framework when...' section to differentiate from shallow SEO comparisons.
